answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind each agent to a canyon of sequential delay proofs, so any attempt to forge a prior identity is computationally infeasible, demanding a VRF preimage and incurring slashing penalties. Staking copper collateral makes identity cloning yield negative expected attack utility, since cloned votes risk forfeiture exceeding forgery reward. Verifiable delay and BFT finality give an information-theoretic defense, enforcing a robust Nash equilibrium where honest sortition dominates Sybil growth.
